subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the durable memory write resolver be owned by memory-core as the active-memory contract, memory-wiki as the belief/claim workflow, memory-lancedb or another memory plugin, or a new plugin SDK seam before implementation starts?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested resolver, but choosing durable schema ownership, conflict semantics, provenance requirements, and operator review UX is a product boundary decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Design active-memory contract first
options.body: Use memory-core or a new active-memory SDK seam as the owner for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history before implementation.

options.title: Route through memory-wiki
options.body: Treat structured claims, contradictions, evidence, and review dashboards as memory-wiki responsibilities while keeping memory-core focused on files, search, promotion, and dreaming.

options.title: Defer durable resolver
options.body: Keep the current Markdown, memory-lancedb, and wiki layers while collecting more production examples before committing to a durable write API.

recommendation.title: Design active-memory contract first
recommendation.body: Use memory-core or a new active-memory SDK seam as the owner for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily an ownership and product-boundary decision across memory-core, memory-wiki, plugin APIs, and durable storage, and he has the strongest available product-boundary signal in the inspected history.
